To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep learning and radiomic features from chest CTs can be used to predict the 5-year mortality of individuals, which has a high impact in preventive and personalized healthcare.

1) we propose new prognoses methods based on chest CT images; 2) we develop a deep learning framework that predicts 5-year mortality with an AUC of 69.8% and accuracy of of 66.5%; 3) we develop a radiomics framework that predicts 4.5-year mortality with accuracy of 64%.
we have developed a novel framework for automated 5-year mortality estimation using deep learning and hand-crafted radiomic features from chest computed CT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new prognostic tools that predict mortality in elderly individuals based on their chest CT images.
developing new methods for predicting 5-year mortality from chest CT images.

the following questions: 1) What are the best deep learning and radiomic models to predict 5-year survival in elderly people using chest CT? and 2) Can we improve the accuracy of 5-year mortality predictions in elderly people using deep learning and/or radiomics? We propose a novel deep learning model that predicts 5-year mortality based on a set of features automatically extracted from chest CT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed models are capable of producing 5-year mortality predictions with a high level of accuracy, and that they are a step forward in the development of automated methods for the early detection of diseases and the prediction of their evolution, with a view to improving the quality of life and reducing the costs of healthcare.
the proposed deep learning models produce a mean 5 year mortality prediction AUC and accuracy that are higher than the ones produced by the radiomics models.
the proposed deep learning models have the potential to be used as a tool for the development of a new generation of personalised healthcare applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel deep learning-based method to predict 5-year all-cause mortality in elderly individuals from chest CT.
the proposed methods have the potential to be used in the early detection of diseases that are associated with high mortality, such as cancer, cardiovascular disease and lung diseases.
we propose new methods to predict 5-year all-cause mortality in elderly individuals based on the analysis of chest CT scans.
The main takeaway from our work is that

deep learning can be successfully applied to predict 5-year survival in elderly individuals using CT scans, with a performance that is comparable to the performance of radiomics, a method that has been used for this task for many years.
deep learning models can learn to predict 5-year all-cause mortality in a single process from chest CT images and segmentation maps of the lungs, heart, aorta and mediastinum.
the use of deep learning and radiomic models can be a promising approach to develop automated tools that can predict mortality in elderly patients using only a chest CT.
